summary: Attacked part 2 of the Representation theory area — AdoIwasawa, CharacterTheory, InductionRestriction, QuiverRepresentations, SchurWeyl and SemisimpleAlgebras, 55 stages in all — on five heads, with the eleven roadmaps of parts 1 and 3 read for what is planned twice. **No findings.** Four promising leads dissolved on inspection and each is recorded below so that the clean result is checkable rather than merely asserted. The two worth naming: the whole area records no stage-level dependency graph, which turns out to be within atlas norms and backed by roadmap-level prerequisites where the mathematics needs them; and the library-boundary head that produced the sibling model-theory area's sharpest finding yields nothing here, because these roadmaps name the exact Mathlib declarations they consume and say why the library result is not enough — SemisimpleAlgebras Layer 6 plans precisely the first open TODO in Mathlib's own BrauerGroup file. On duplication, the highest cross-part vocabulary overlap is 0.286 and the one substantive pair is complementary by explicit design.
checked: Every stage of all six roadmaps, with its document: AdoIwasawa 10, CharacterTheory 10, InductionRestriction 10, QuiverRepresentations 7, SchurWeyl 10, SemisimpleAlgebras 8 — 55 in all.

Eligibility, measured rather than assumed. Of the 43 papers this session has reviewed, none routes to any of these six roadmaps. I computed this across every available area red team before choosing: six areas have zero entanglement and the arithmetic-geometry ones reach 13, so this area was picked to keep the red team independent of my own reviewing. I did verify RT-AREA-representations-1, the sibling part, in the immediately preceding job, which is the cross-part context PROTOCOL section 17 asks a part to have rather than a conflict, since parts 2 and 3 are different roadmaps.

The dependency graph, and a lead it raised that dissolved. All 55 stages have empty `requires` and empty `consumers`, where the sibling part records 25 `requires` edges across its 41 stages. Not a defect: these stages carry no prose Inputs paragraph either, so unlike LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.0-LD.2 there is no prose-versus-field mismatch to report; prerequisites are recorded at roadmap level and are present where the mathematics needs them (CharacterTheory declares InductionRestriction, SchurWeyl and SemisimpleAlgebras; QuiverRepresentations declares RootSystems and SemisimpleAlgebras); and empty `requires` is atlas-normal at 669 of 1962 stages, 34 per cent.

Stage numbering, which looked irregular and is not. SemisimpleAlgebras appears to hold a 'layer-15' between layers 1 and 2, which is the slug of Layer 1.5, 'every simple module is a minimal left ideal'; InductionRestriction likewise carries Layers 3a and 3b. Deliberate sub-numbering, not a gap.

A second lead that dissolved, on direction. InductionRestriction, SchurWeyl and SemisimpleAlgebras each cite CharacterTheory in their stage prose without declaring it a prerequisite, which reads as three missing prerequisites until one checks which way the arrow points: CharacterTheory declares all three as its own prerequisites, so those citations name a consumer, not a dependency, and declaring CharacterTheory would invert the dependency and create a cycle.

The library boundary, target by target, which is the head that produced the model-theory area's second finding (LD.0 instructing a worker to construct ultraproducts and prove Los's theorem when Mathlib has both). Confirmed in Mathlib at the pin: Maschke (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Maschke.lean), IsSemisimpleRing, Wedderburn-Artin material, and BrauerGroup (Mathlib/Algebra/BrauerGroup/Defs.lean); not found, and so correctly planned, a Specht-module file (SchurWeyl Layer 3) or a Krull-Schmidt theorem (QuiverRepresentations Layer 2). No layer plans what the library already has, and two are unusually precise about it. SemisimpleAlgebras Layer 2 opens 'From `IsSemisimpleRing.exists_ringEquiv_pi_matrix_divisionRing` ... pin a `WedderburnPresentation R`' and then states the reason the library theorem does not finish the job: 'Because Mathlib's theorem is existential, this object carries arbitrary choices and is not the source of the invariants.' SemisimpleAlgebras Layer 6 says 'Consume `IsBrauerEquivalent`, `Brauer.CSA_Setoid`, `BrauerGroup`. Build the `CommGroup` structure on `BrauerGroup K`', and Mathlib's own BrauerGroup/Defs.lean lists as TODO 1 'Prove that the Brauer group is an abelian group where multiplication is defined as tensor product' — the layer plans exactly the library's open TODO.

Omissions, and a third lead that dissolved. Brauer characters, block theory, defect groups and decomposition matrices appear nowhere in either roadmap directory; the only three roadmaps matching 'modular representation' (SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation, GL2ModularityLifting, AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights) use the phrase in the arithmetic sense of a residual modular representation, and none of them declares any of the six as a prerequisite, so nothing consumes this area needing modular representation theory of finite groups. The area is also deliberately ordinary theory rather than silently incomplete: CharacterTheory works under `char` not dividing `|G|` and over the complex numbers, proves that ordinary character values lie in the cyclotomic field, and mentions Brauer only for the splitting-field theorem, flagged 'off the critical path'. Its other use of the word modular is the modular reduction step of the Dixon-Schneider algorithm, not modular representation theory. A topic the atlas has not chosen to plan is not the same as a topic this area leaves out.

Duplication across the three parts, against the eleven roadmaps of parts 1 and 3 (ReductiveGroups, RootSystems, ClassicalGroups, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, ReductiveGroupsPartII, RepresentationTheory, CompactGroups, LieGroups, LieHighestWeight, SpinRepresentations, ZigzagPreprojective). The highest cross-part vocabulary overlap is 0.286 (AdoIwasawa against LieHighestWeight), below the 0.33 threshold, and these are whole-roadmap scores that shared background vocabulary inflates.

The one cross-part pair worth reading rather than scoring: SchurWeyl Layer 9, 'Schur-Weyl duality for the orthogonal and symplectic groups (the Brauer algebra)', against part 3's SpinRepresentations. They are complementary by explicit design, and SpinRepresentations says so in its own summary: 'The spin representations are the one part of the finite-dimensional representation theory of the classical groups that the tensor-power engine cannot reach. Every irreducible representation of GL_n and SL_n is cut out of a tensor power ... and so is every irreducible of Sp_n; for the orthogonal series this is false.' SpinRepresentations exists because the tensor-power engine that SchurWeyl builds cannot reach it, and it declares ClassicalGroups, LieHighestWeight and RootSystems as prerequisites. The neighbouring pair ClassicalGroups against SchurWeyl is likewise pinned in the sources, ClassicalGroups Layer 2 stating that '../SchurWeyl owns the group algebra C[S_a], the Young symmetrizer c_lambda, and Schur-Weyl ...'.

The stage `status` field, calibrated before treating it as a defect. All 55 stages carry status 'unknown'; atlas-wide that value covers 656 of 1962 stages, 33 per cent, and the only other value in use is 'needs_source_decomposition'. The count of stages with empty `requires` (669) is close to the count with status 'unknown' (656), which is consistent with both marking stages not yet decomposed. Within norms, not a finding.
